stops.title: Ground-Level Hazard

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: People have been walking around it all morning. Someone will clean it later.

cordon_off.feedback: You controlled the risk instead of stepping around it. Alex moves to cordon off the spill area.

report_only.feedback: Reporting is right, but the walkway stayed open in the meantime. Alex moves to a safe observation position.

ignore.feedback: A hazard was normalized because it had been there all morning. Alex follows Dave, accepting the unsafe condition.

stops.learning_objective: Do not normalize common workplace hazards.

stops.title: Zone 02 | Blind-Corner Forklift Traffic

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: Don't slow down here, the forklift drivers know to watch out for foot traffic. Just keep moving.

hold_position.feedback: You waited with Dave until the driver safely braked and cleared the intersection. Holding position prevents blind-corner collisions. Alex holds position.

proceed_carefully.feedback: Proceeding while waving at the driver is risky because tall cargo blocks driver sightlines. Alex moves cautiously.

walk_straight_through.feedback: Walking straight through without stopping triggered a dangerous forklift near-miss! Never assume an operator has sight of pedestrians.

stops.learning_objective: Never assume an operator has seen you; hold position until eye contact or clear path is established.

stops.title: Bent Rack Upright

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: That's been bent since before I started here. It's fine, it's not going anywhere.

cordon_off.feedback: You restricted access and flagged it for a structural inspection. A bent upright can fail without warning under load. Alex moves to cordon off the damaged bay.

report_only.feedback: Reporting is right, but the aisle stayed in use while you waited for someone to act on it. Alex moves to a safe distance while reporting.

ignore.feedback: Because it had looked that way for as long as anyone could remember, it had stopped registering as damage at all. Alex follows Dave past the structural risk.

stops.learning_objective: Challenge structural damage that's been normalized by familiarity.

stops.title: Charging Bay Warning Light

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: Charger's fine, we've had worse close calls than a blinking light. Someone will swap that battery out eventually.

cordon_off.feedback: You pulled the combustibles clear and flagged the charger as out of service until the indicator was checked. An early warning sign got treated like the warning it was. Alex moves to secure the charging bay.

report_only.feedback: Reporting the fault was right, but the combustibles stayed within reach of the charging point while you waited. Alex moves to a safe position while reporting.

ignore.feedback: A blinking indicator and a stack of boxes both got treated as background noise, the same way Dave already had. Alex follows Dave past the fire risk.

stops.learning_objective: Early warning indicators are hazards in progress, not decoration.

stops.title: Clear Aisle Check

supervisor.name: Dave
supervisor.dialogue: This one's clean, always is. Main aisle, good sightlines, nothing stored where it shouldn't be.

continue_on.feedback: You checked it yourself, agreed with Dave's read, and moved on without turning a clear aisle into a paperwork exercise. Alex continues the patrol with confidence.

report_only.feedback: Flagging a genuinely clear aisle isn't wrong, but treating every stop as something to escalate has its own cost. Alex moves to file the unnecessary report.

stops.learning_objective: Not everything needs escalating; over-reporting has a cost.

endOfSessionRules.feedback: Two separate warning signs went unaddressed. On their own, either might have stayed a near miss. Together, they became the incident report Dave was hoping to avoid.
